title: Capacity cartography: reservations + burst timeline wireframe notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working set of UX notes and rough wireframe descriptions for the Dedicated Capacity console view we call 'Capacity Cartography' — a single surface for visualizing GPU pool reservations, burst windows, autoscale policies, and ad-hoc (ephemeral) allocations. Aim: make it trivial for platform owners to see what capacity is reserved vs. available, how bursts and autoscale interact, and to create/modify reservations with clear cost/impact previews.

Audience:
- Platform engineers who manage Dedicated GPU pools
- Solutions engineers preparing reserved allocations for customers
- Product owners evaluating rollout of reservation automation

Primary goals (top-level):
1) Visual timeline of reservations + bursts across pools (1 day -> 90 day scope).
2) Reservation builder that prevents conflicts and surfaces cost and routing impact before commit.
3) Clear autoscale policy editor integrated with reservation semantics.
4) Lightweight mobile-friendly reservation inspector for on-call.

High-level constraints / design principles:
- Timeline should be readable at glance: color lanes per pool, reservation cards stacked vertically, bursts as translucent overlays.
- Avoid modal stacking. Reservation builder uses a right-side panel (drawer) with live validation and cost preview.
- Everything editable in-place where possible (rename, extend, shrink reservation).
- Make fallback behavior explicit: if a reservation overlaps a higher-priority commitment, show suggested fallback routes and estimated latency impact.
- Accessible color palette for statuses (reserved, available, burst, error). Use color + icon + pattern for colorblind safety.

Main screens / components (wireframe descriptions):
1) Capacity Cartography Landing (desktop)- Top nav: project selector (org/team), date-range quick selector (24h, 7d, 30d, 90d), pool filter (checkboxes), search (reservation id / owner).- Left column (narrow): pool list summary with aggregated metrics (pool name, gpu SKU, reserved v available GPUs, 95th latency SLA indicator). Each pool row is clickable to focus on that lane.- Center: timeline canvas. X-axis time. Y-axis lanes = pools.- Reservation cards: rectangular blocks with left-aligned owner initials, title (reservation name), card badge for type (recurring, one-off, burst), hours/dates, and small cost-per-hour figure. Hover reveals quick actions: Edit, Split, Cancel, View Commit.- Burst overlay: a semi-transparent band across the lane with a lightning bolt icon. When hovered, a popover shows burst policy (max GPUs, max minutes/day, current usage).- Autoscale band: dashed region representing policy range (min -> target -> max). When autoscale is active on top of a reservation, show stacked glyphs.- Right rail: reservation inspector. When a card is clicked, inspector shows full details, commit terms, linked customer/account, and telemetry preview (expected token-hours/day). Also an impact preview button that simulates: if we cancel or trim this reservation, what will be routed to which pool/model?

2) Reservation builder (right-side drawer, multi-step inline)- Step 1: Basics: name, owner, pool selector (dropdown with SKU and region), start+end (calendar + quick presets), recurrence (none | daily | weekly | cron-like).- Step 2: Capacity spec: GPU SKU, instance count (slider with min/max), fallback pools (multi-select with priority ordering). Live validation shows conflicts (red badge) or approvals required.- Step 3: Autoscale & burst: pick autoscale preset (conservative | cost-lean | aggressive) or configure custom rules (metric, scale-out threshold, cooldowns). Burst checkbox: enable ephemeral bursts with max GPUs and per-day budget. Show a small graph of theoretical token-cost curve.- Step 4: Cost & commit: detailed cost preview (hourly cost, estimated monthly cost, credits usage), SLA impact, and required approvers (if > X GPUs or > $Y/month). Action buttons: Save as draft, Request approval, Commit now.

Microcopy & inline help examples:
- Reservation name placeholder: 'Research - LLM fine-tune (Q2)'.
- Conflict tooltip: 'Overlaps with "Acme enterprise commit" (priority: reserved). Click Suggest to auto-shift to nearest available window.'
- Burst tooltip: 'Burst capacity is ephemeral and billed at burst rate. Bursts do not change committed SLA.'
- Autoscale help: 'Autoscale only scales within the reservation bounds unless fallback pools are configured.'

Conflict resolution flows (UX):
- Auto-suggest shift: If user picks a time range that conflicts with higher-priority reservation, show suggested non-overlapping windows with exact shift minutes. Accepting auto-suggest will pre-fill the builder with new dates and show delta in cost.- Split reservation: allow splitting an existing reservation into two contiguous reservations. Use small inline handles on the card edges; dragging opens mini-surface to confirm split.- Force-queue: for low-priority ad-hoc requests we show a queue card pinned to top of lane with ETA estimation based on current active usage and configured burst budgets.

Edge cases and validation rules (grooming notes):
- If a reservation references SKUs that are removed from a pool: block commit and show migration wizard.
- Overlapping recurring reservations with different recurrence patterns: display next 3 occurrences and require explicit manual resolution if > 50% overlap.
- Approver workflow: if commit requires approval, reservation state = 'pending-approval' and timeline card has diagonal hatch. Pending items should be filterable.

Telemetry / events to emit (for product + infra):
- ui.reservation.builder.open
- ui.reservation.validate.conflict (payload: reservationId, conflictingId)
- ui.reservation.commit.request
- ui.reservation.commit.success
- ui.reservation.modify.split
- ui.timeline.zoom.change
- ui.burst.preview.activate
Include these names in the PR so backend can hook audit logs.

Accessibility considerations:
- Keyboard focus order: pool list -> timeline -> inspector -> builder drawer controls.
- Avoid relying on color alone for status. Use icons and dense textual labels for small screens.
- All critical actions (commit, cancel) require an explicit confirmation checkbox and keyboard-accessible modal.

Mobile / narrow viewport variant (notes):
- Collapsed top: project + date selector.
- Show only 1 pool lane at a time; swipe left/right to move between pools.
- Timeline condensed into scrollable timeline with stacked cards; clicking opens inspector full-screen.
- Builder becomes full-screen stepper.

Example user flow (happy path):
1) Platform owner filters to 'us-west-2, A100-80GB' pool.
2) Sees a gap in timeline for April 14-16. Clicks 'Reserve' button.
3) Builder pre-fills suggested cost and shows a suggested fallback to 'A10G-pool-1' if demand spikes.
4) Owner sets autoscale preset 'cost-lean', enables burst for 2 hours/day and commits.
5) Reservation card appears with green badge and email notification queued to approver if required.

Backlog grooming (prioritized items):
- MUST: timeline canvas skeleton + pool lanes + click-to-open inspector (RED-5912).
- SHOULD: right-side builder drawer with live validation and cost preview (depends on pricing API).
- SHOULD: autoscale presets & burst overlay semantics.
- NICE-TO-HAVE: smart suggestions for shifting conflicts using simulated optimizer (low confidence, separate spike queue).
- TKT: split/merge reservation UX and edge-case scheduler tests.
- TKT: mobile stepper optimization and swipe-to-change-pool.

Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- Timeline shows correct reserved vs available GPUs for selected pools for 30-day window with <= 2% mismatch against scheduler snapshot data.
- Reservation builder blocks commits that violate SKU availability and surfaces at least one automated suggestion.
- Cost preview updates within 2 seconds of any change to capacity sliders.
- All emitted telemetry events are logged to the audit stream.

Open questions for PM/infra:
- Do we allow negative-cost credits to be applied to burst billing (accounting edge)? Ticketed at JIRA-RED-6021.
- Exact approval thresholds for auto-approvals (product to confirm).
- Backend API shape for conflict-simulate endpoint — returns candidate windows or adjustments? (need contract before building suggest button).

Next steps / action items:
- @Liam: mock desktop timeline canvas tiles for review (due 2026-03-16).
- @Priya: validate cost API latency for cost preview (due 2026-03-12).
- @Marcus: sketch mobile stepper + swipe interactions (due 2026-03-18).
- Sync agenda: capacity-cartography design sync 2026-03-11 (include infra, product, UX).

Raw sketch notes (ascii thumbnails for quick reference):
- Timeline lane: [Pool name] | ----[Reservation A]---- | | [Burst band^] |----[Reservation B]----|
- Reservation card (compact): [AV] Research-fin-llm | 4x A100 | Apr 14-16 | $12/hr

Unresolved UX debates (notes):
- Inline split handles vs. separate 'split' flow: inline is faster but risk of accidental splits on mobile.
- Visual density: provide a compact mode for SREs who want maximum timeline density.

If you review, please add comments inline or mark sections with 'ACCEPT / REJECT / NEEDS INFO'. This doc is intentionally informal — use it to seed a formal spec once flows are settled.

End of file.
